arrangements: Snowflake: place Star tiles on the middle row and rotate the outer paths toward the center.
Dragon: make a stepped chain, using Comet tails as the spine and one Crescent as a curled head.
Crown: make a three-tile base with three upward points suggested by alternating Star and Crescent centers.
Pocket mosaic: return all nine to the exact three-by-three reference storage field.
assumptions: The nine tiles are printed from a common rigid FDM filament with a 0.4 mm nozzle and placed rather than mechanically locked.
A 98.5 mm square mosaic is pocket-small relative to a common 220 mm printer bed, though no specific pocket or container fit is claimed.

components.form: Rounded-square reversible tile with recessed edge gates and crescent dimple field.
components.interfaces: Four universal 1.8 mm centered edge gates for loose visual/tactile registration.
components.name: Crescent tile family
components.placement: Three occurrences in the 3×3 mosaic; freely movable during play.
components.purpose: Curves four spaced dimples into a tactile lunar arc and supplies one-pip family identification.

components.form: Rounded-square reversible tile with recessed edge gates and comet dimple field.
components.interfaces: Four universal 1.8 mm centered edge gates for loose visual/tactile registration.
components.name: Comet tile family
components.placement: Three occurrences in the 3×3 mosaic; freely movable during play.
components.purpose: Uses a descending four-dimple trail and two-pip family identification to suggest direction and a dragon spine.

components.form: Rounded-square reversible tile with recessed edge gates and star dimple field.
components.interfaces: Four universal 1.8 mm centered edge gates for loose visual/tactile registration.
components.name: Star tile family
components.placement: Three occurrences in the 3×3 mosaic; freely movable during play.
components.purpose: Uses a center plus five orbiting dimples and three-pip family identification to create radial anchors.

concept.intended_interaction: A player gathers three separately printed copies of each tile family into the compact storage mosaic, then lays, rotates, and flips the nine tiles edge-to-edge so the centered gates weave continuous paths into suggested creatures, crowns, snowflakes, and invented constellations.
concept.interaction: Lay, rotate, and flip the nine tiles. Begin with the compact three-by-three mosaic, then let connected paths suggest a six-point snowflake, a long comet-dragon, a crown, or a new named constellation. Connections are loose edge-to-edge placement with broad registration channels, never snaps.
concept.signature_decision: Use one universal centered edge-gate geometry on all four sides of every tile, while three spaced rounded-dimple constellations create Crescent, Comet, and Star identities on both faces. Compatibility is therefore invariant under family, quarter-turn rotation, and flipping without snaps.
concept.summary: Nine chunky reversible tiles form a pocket field of continuous starlight paths. Three tactile families—Crescent, Comet, and Star—share one exact centered edge gate, so every quarter-turn or flip preserves a graceful line into the next tile while the interior symbols redirect it differently.
concept.title: Night-Sky Weave
unresolved_risks: Bottom-face recess bridging, tactile delight, repeated handling wear, and first-time pattern discovery require physical or human testing not performed in Spark.
Loose placement intentionally trades structural retention for immediate rearrangement.

decisions: A 31.5 mm tile is broad enough for a full-thumb grip while three tiles plus two 2.0 mm gaps remain under 100 mm square.
A 5.6 mm body with 1.2 mm recesses from both faces leaves a 3.2 mm continuous core; both the tactile step and core remain above a 0.8 mm two-line minimum for a 0.4 mm nozzle.
All four edges terminate at one centered 1.8 mm gate; compatibility is exact and independent of motif family, rotation, or flip.

Spaced rounded dimple constellations carry the visual and tactile distinctions in monochrome, while short rounded edge gates meet neighboring tiles. Every material land between pockets is at least two nozzle lines; no motif depends on paint, sharp cusps, or tiny raised fins.
The pieces print flat with no purchased hardware. Bottom recess spans are limited to 1.8 mm, treated as short self-bridges rather than support-demanding cavities.
Loose placement avoids brittle snaps; the repeated centered gates and rounded tile perimeter provide gentle geometric registration.
limitations: Digital geometry checks do not prove physical print quality, tactile delight, durability, or first-time player response.
The tiles align by placement rather than locking, so a completed constellation is intentionally easy to rearrange.
research.method: Wish-specific deliberate design choices under Tess Loop's host-bound method; no external dimensions or purchased components are required.
